context: Decide repo-wide whether distribute_by holds rendered SQL or a summary value, then make every generator consistent with that choice (Redshift/Synapse currently render; StarRocks/Doris/Firebolt currently summarize). If it becomes rendered SQL, give TuningClauses a platform-aware clause order so StarRocks emits DISTRIBUTED BY after PARTITION BY. Update the pinned snapshot tests to match the decision rather than working around them.
description:
chatgpt-codex-connector review finding on merged PR #1262 (P2, benchbox/core/tuning/generators/starrocks.py:180). Deferred from the PR-review sweep in PR #1292 because the clean fix requires a repo-wide contract decision, not a local patch; tracked in GitHub issue #1293.

When a StarRocks tuning config includes distribution, the generator stores the BARE COLUMN NAME in clauses.distribute_by AND appends the rendered 'DISTRIBUTED BY HASH(...)' to additional_clauses. The dry-run path (_build_table_ddl_entry -> TuningClauses.get_inline_clauses()) treats distribute_by itself as an inline SQL clause before appending additional_clauses, so StarRocks dry-run previews contain a stray line like 'l_orderkey' plus the real distribution clause, and no longer match the execution DDL.
Thread: https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/pull/1262#discussion_r3630404241

Why this is not a drive-by fix (verified 2026-07-24):
- get_inline_clauses() is owned by the SHARED TuningClauses dataclass (benchbox/core/tuning/ddl_generator.py), NOT by the generator class, so there is no StarRocks-only override seam.
- 6+ tests pin the bare column as intentional: tests/unit/core/tuning/test_starrocks_ddl_generator.py and test_renderer_snapshot_starrocks.py assert distribute_by == 'l_orderkey'.
- Doris (generators/doris.py:478) and Firebolt (generators/firebolt.py:149) also store non-clause values in distribute_by, while Redshift and Synapse store fully rendered clauses ('DISTSTYLE KEY\nDISTKEY (col)', 'HASH([col])').
- get_inline_clauses() emits distribute_by BEFORE partition_by, but StarRocks requires DISTRIBUTED BY after PARTITION BY, so naively promoting the rendered clause into distribute_by produces invalid DDL ordering.

anti_patterns.dont: promote the rendered clause into distribute_by without fixing clause order
anti_patterns.why: get_inline_clauses() emits distribute_by before partition_by, which is invalid StarRocks DDL

anti_patterns.dont: special-case StarRocks by deleting the pinned test assertions
anti_patterns.instead: make the contract decision explicit and update the tests to the new contract with a rationale
anti_patterns.why: those tests encode the current intentional contract; silently flipping them hides the decision

preserves.behavior: Dry-run preview and execution DDL agree for every platform after the change
Redshift and Azure Synapse rendered DISTSTYLE/HASH clauses keep producing byte-identical execution DDL

verifications.description: Dry-run preview matches execution DDL for StarRocks

work_units.summary: Audit every generator's distribute_by usage (redshift, azure_synapse, firebolt, doris, starrocks) and decide rendered-SQL vs summary; record the decision
Make all generators consistent with the decision, including clause ordering so StarRocks emits DISTRIBUTED BY after PARTITION BY
Update the pinned StarRocks snapshot/generator tests to the decided contract and assert dry-run preview matches execution DDL
